claims.text: Room-temperature L-PBF of AlCrFeNiSi is prone to rapid cooling, compositional segregation, high residual stress, and defect formation.
Preheating the L-PBF build substrate reduces the thermal gradient between the molten pool and substrate.
A substrate temperature of approximately 200°C is an appropriate preheating intervention for AlCrFeNiSi.
Substrate preheating lowers the solidification cooling rate.
Lower thermal gradients and cooling rates mitigate residual-stress accumulation.
Lower thermal gradients and cooling rates minimize elemental segregation in L-PBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Substrate preheating reduces defects such as hot cracking in L-PBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Preheated samples will have lower residual stress than samples fabricated on a room-temperature substrate.
Preheated samples will exhibit more homogeneous microstructures and less segregation than samples fabricated on a room-temperature substrate.
Preheated samples will exhibit higher tensile strength and toughness than samples fabricated on a room-temperature substrate.
Laser power and scan speed are important L-PBF process parameters affecting processability and performance.
L-PBF energy-density adjustment can produce parts with density exceeding 99%.
The proposed intervention is effective for AlCrFeNiSi when part density exceeds approximately 99%.
The intervention remains effective at moderate preheat temperatures up to about 400°C.
The intervention may become less effective when energy density is substantially outside typical L-PBF values or thermal management is otherwise altered.
